**DynaLM 0.3.0.** DynaLM's own CPU engine, measured against llama.cpp and Ollama on a fixed CPU benchmark (CPU suite v1). It is verified on macOS on Apple Silicon (one Apple M4 Pro). The Linux and Windows builds are CI-tested: built and tested in CI without real models.

## Overview

DynaLM runs large language models locally, on the CPU or the GPU, as one program with no Python. It provides `dynalm run`, `chat` and `serve`, and an OpenAI-compatible HTTP API with streaming. This release is about the CPU: DynaLM's own kernels now run the CPU path on Apple M4 class CPUs, with no ggml code in it.

## Main improvements

- **Native CPU engine:**
  - Quantized matmul kernels (`qmm`) with NEON dot-product and i8mm.
  - An SME tier for prompt processing on CPUs with SME (Apple M4 class).
  - NEON attention kernels.
  - Builds with `DYNALM_NATIVE_ONLY=ON` contain no ggml or llama.cpp code; `tools/ci/check_native.sh` checks a build for it.
- **Default CPU path on SME CPUs:** on Apple M4 class CPUs, `--backend cpu` (and `auto` when no GPU runs the model) uses DynaLM's kernels. `--backend ggml-cpu` still selects ggml's. Other CPUs keep ggml's kernels as the default, because DynaLM's kernels have not been measured there.
- **Decode:** decode steps are 15–21% faster than in the previous development build, from larger, balanced work chunks.
- **CPU scheduling:** on SME CPUs, prompts are processed in 512-token bursts while decoding streams wait (at most 2 s; `DYNALM_PREFILL_BURST_MS`).
- **CPU memory:** after a weight is repacked, the file pages of the original are released. The CPU prefix cache keeps at most a quarter of the KV pool.
- **`--execution auto`** (new default): compiled execution on GPUs and on CPUs with qmm kernels.

## Supported environment

| Artifact | Platform | Validation for this release |
|---|---|---|
| `dynalm-macos-arm64.tar.gz` | macOS on Apple Silicon, CPU and Metal | **Verified** on one Apple M4 Pro: full test suite, AddressSanitizer, UBSan and ThreadSanitizer runs, accuracy against llama.cpp, CPU suite v1 |
| `dynalm-macos-x86_64.tar.gz` | macOS on Intel, CPU | **CI-tested:** built and tested in CI under Rosetta (model-free tests) |
| `dynalm-linux-x86_64.tar.gz`, `dynalm-linux-arm64.tar.gz` | Linux, CPU | **CI-tested:** built, tested (model-free) and fresh-install checked in CI. x86-64 was also built and tested with GCC 13 and Clang 18 in an x86-64 container; not checked with real models |
| `dynalm-windows-x86_64.zip`, `dynalm-windows-arm64.zip` | Windows, CPU | **CI-tested:** as Linux |

- **Vulkan and CUDA are experimental**, as in 0.2.0.
- **The fast CPU path needs SME.** Apple M1–M3 and other ARM and x86 CPUs run ggml's CPU kernels by default, as in 0.2.0.

## Performance and accuracy

All results are from one Apple M4 Pro (24 GB, AC power, Energy Mode Automatic). The build was strict native (`macos-native`), with DynaLM's CPU kernels, the same ones the release package runs on this CPU.

**CPU suite v1** (`docs/perf/cpu-suite-v1.md`):
- Models: Qwen2.5-1.5B and Qwen3-4B, Q4_K_M.
- Output: 128 tokens, greedy.
- 4,096 tokens of context per user.
- 5 rounds; ratio per workload = median over the rounds.
- Every request returned all 128 tokens.

| Workload | vs llama.cpp |
|---|---|
| C1 1.5B, 1 user, 128-token prompt: output tokens/s | 1.08× |
| C2 1.5B, 1 user, 2,048-token prompt: whole request | 1.78× |
| C3 1.5B, 4 users: total tokens/s | 1.95× |
| C4 1.5B, 8 users: total tokens/s | 1.68× |
| C5 1.5B, 8 users: 95th-percentile token gap | 1.19× |
| C6 4B, 1 user, 512-token prompt: output tokens/s | 1.46× |
| C7 4B, 1 user, 2,048-token prompt: first token | 2.26× |
| C8 4B, 1 user, 2,048-token prompt: token gap | 1.23× |
| **Geometric mean** | **1.53×** |

- **Against Ollama:** 1.53× over C6–C8. Ollama stops early on the 1.5B model despite `ignore_eos`, so C1–C5 are not comparable.
- **Peak server memory:**

  | Model | DynaLM | llama.cpp | Ollama |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 1.5B | 1,508 MiB | 4,118 MiB (2.73×) | 3,496 MiB (2.32×) |
  | 4B | 3,944 MiB | 11,403 MiB (2.89×) | 8,949 MiB (2.27×) |

**Accuracy against llama.cpp** (same GGUF files, teacher-forced on 20 × 512 tokens of wikitext-2):

| Model | Next-token agreement | Mean KL |
|---|---|---|
| 1.5B | 100% | 1.7e-7 |
| 4B | 100% | 4.0e-7 |

This measures agreement with llama.cpp, not answer quality.

## Known limitations

- **Measured on one Apple M4 Pro only.** No other CPU was benchmarked; there are no x86 performance results.
- **The project's 2× target is not met.** Single-user decode is 1.08–1.46× llama.cpp.
- **8 users on Qwen3-4B on the CPU:** token gaps reach about 1 s while new 512-token prompts are processed.
- Linux and Windows inference with real models has not been validated for this release.

## Installation

Linux and macOS:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dynalm-project/dynalm/main/scripts/install.sh | sh
dynalm --version   # DynaLM   0.3.0
```

Windows (PowerShell): `irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dynalm-project/dynalm/main/scripts/install.ps1 | iex`. Each archive is listed in `SHA256SUMS` and carries signed build provenance: `gh attestation verify <file> --repo dynalm-project/dynalm`. To build from source, see `docs/build.md`.

## Changes and compatibility

- **On Apple M4 class CPUs, `--backend cpu` now runs DynaLM's kernels.** For ggml's kernels, use `--backend ggml-cpu`.
- **Default thread count on hybrid CPUs:** DynaLM's CPU kernels (qmm, ARM) now use the performance cores only, as ggml's kernels do; that is how CPU suite v1 was measured. `--threads N` overrides.
- **`--execution` default is now `auto`.** `reference` keeps the previous behaviour.
- **New presets** `macos-native` and `linux-native` (strict native, no ggml).
- **New environment variables:**
  - `DYNALM_PREFILL_BURST_MS` (`0` turns prefill bursts off);
  - `DYNACORE_SME=0` (no SME tier);
  - `DYNACORE_QMM_RELEASE_SOURCE=0` (keep the original weight pages);
  - `DYNACORE_GEMV_CHUNK_KB` (decode chunk size, for measurements).
